evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform docs
evidence.finding: Official docs distinguish foundational/custom/external agents and flows, available tiers and credit consumption. Different components and feature flags have separate availability.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform external-agents
evidence.locator: External agents; Quickstart; Access credentials; Security considerations
evidence.finding: Managed Claude Code/Codex integrate through GitLab credentials, while Amazon Q/Gemini require user credentials. External-agent access is restricted to verified customers/flags and has weaker network isolation than native flows.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform external-examples-current
evidence.locator: Integrated with GitLab, Claude Code and OpenAI Codex YAML
evidence.finding: Exact adapter examples install @anthropic-ai/claude-code and @openai/codex and invoke claude -p or codex exec with GitLab gateway configuration and authenticated glab. These are coding harnesses, not provider model aliases.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform developer-current
evidence.locator: Generate MR from issue; Agentic Chat; GitLab Duo CLI; prerequisites
evidence.finding: Developer Flow turns issue/workplan/context into code/merge requests, can be mentioned in discussions, uses AI Sessions and runs locally through the product-owned Duo CLI. Feature-specific version/flag prerequisites apply.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform sessions
evidence.finding: AI Sessions lists live work, allows cancel and checkpoint approve/reject/modify and retains sessions 30 days after last activity. Interaction resets the retention period.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform workspace-subagents
evidence.locator: History; When to use; Create/delegate; result return
evidence.finding: Workspace subagents are GA in 19.6 for Developer Flow, with repository Markdown prompt/tool definitions, separate conversations and result-only return to the parent. UI delegation/return rows and CLI Ctrl+T expose the child work.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform automations
evidence.locator: History; Event types; Scheduled automations history and limits
evidence.finding: Event automations are GA; schedules are 19.6-enabled beta under flags, limited to custom flows/Developer Flow. Event and scheduled identities differ, and unsupported flow/event combinations fail.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform execution
evidence.locator: Executor architecture; runners; Docker executor; execution sandbox requirements
evidence.finding: UI flows execute headless GitLab Duo CLI in CI/CD runners. GitLab.com offers hosted runners and users may configure their own Docker-capable runners. SRT sandbox needs image/namespace support and can fail open with a warning; setup scripts run outside it.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform credits
evidence.locator: Credits usage; For the Free tier; temporary evaluation; commitments; on-demand
evidence.finding: Agent Platform uses credit-based billing, separate from Duo Pro/Enterprise add-on billing. Included credits depend on paid tier; Free can buy commitment credits; temporary evaluation credits expire after 30 days; on-demand bills$1/credit monthly.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform data-usage
evidence.locator: Telemetry; Share group usage data with GitLab; Agent Platform usage data
evidence.finding: Docs disclose aggregated/de-identified Snowplow usage metrics and a separate opt-in group/instance control for full AI interactions. That control is not proof that it stops every telemetry class.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform roadmap
evidence.locator: Monthly releases; latest release; What is coming
evidence.finding: Official direction page currently presents platform 19.6 dated 2026-11-19 and upcoming Plan items. Upcoming titles are not shipped facts and not all have a resolved selected-comparison classification.

evidence.title: GitLab Duo Agent Platform orbit-release
evidence.finding: Dated announcement makes Orbit GA for Premium/Ultimate starting on GitLab.com, with other offerings described separately. This is platform maintenance/context, not a capability/performance test.

evidence.locator: About example runs; September 20,2026, GitLab.com19.5.0-pre; screenshots
evidence.finding: Official cookbook documents actual sample Sessions for Verified issue-to-MR flow with exact session/issue/MR references and version. It is a sample custom flow, not default behavior of every foundational flow.
